## 1. Sri Lanka reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF on the seventh review of the four‑year Extended Fund Facility.

The deal would unlock <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">SDR 254 million</span> (the IMF’s accounting unit, with a value linked to a basket of major currencies) worth about $345 million, raising cumulative disbursements to roughly <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$2.7bn</span> once the Executive Board signs off. Board approval depends on tabling a 2027 Budget consistent with programme parameters and completing a financing assurances review.

The Fund said real GDP expanded <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">4.2% year‑on‑year in the second quarter</span> after eleven straight quarters of growth, while headline inflation ran at 8% in September compared with single‑digit targets. Gross official reserves stood at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$6.9 billion</span> at end‑August, but the IMF flagged risks from the Middle East war and urged cost‑recovery energy pricing.

## 2. The Government presented the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill to Parliament.

The draft replaces the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">1979 PTA</span> (Prevention of Terrorism Act — a security law allowing extended detention without trial), expands search powers and permits <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">detention on order by the Defence Secretary</span> for up to a year. It also creates publication offences with exemptions for fair reporting, academic and artistic work, and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">legitimate political discourse</span>.

Human rights groups said definitions remained overbroad and UN experts warned of inconsistency with international standards on free association and due process. The committee stage offers scope to tighten judicial oversight and refine provisions affecting media, protest and movement.

## 3. The Government moved to address fuel queues and said it would seek legal advice on private suppliers that cut deliveries.

The Energy Minister told Parliament that private operators had <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">reduced daily diesel issues</span> by up to two‑thirds, forcing the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Ceylon Petroleum Corporation</span> (CPC — the state fuel supplier) to lift its release from <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">3,074 to 3,900 tonnes</span> a day. Officials said contracts and the Ministry’s powers under the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">CPC Act</span> would be reviewed at a meeting at the Presidential Secretariat.

The CPC Chairman cited panic buying and social‑media rumours as amplifiers of queues and said no price revision was planned for three months if global conditions hold. Unions urged abolishing private licences, but the current framework allows operators to adjust prices under a formula.

## 4. The World Bank said Sri Lanka’s economy returned to pre‑crisis size but recovery was uneven and poverty remained elevated.

Its Sri Lanka Development Update projected <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">4.4% growth in 2026</span>, with a moderation to 4.2% in 2027 as the rebound fades and productivity constraints bite. The Bank estimated poverty at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">16.9%</span>, above pre‑crisis levels, and warned of exposure to global energy shocks and El Niño.

It urged a pivot from state‑led spending to private investment, exports and productivity, highlighting the broader agrifood system as about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">one‑sixth of GDP</span> and more than two‑fifths of jobs. Recommendations included repurposing subsidies toward research, climate‑smart tech and logistics, and anchoring revenue gains in a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">medium‑term tax strategy</span>.

## 5. The Energy Minister told Parliament inferior coal imports caused a Rs. 15.765 billion loss.

He said the National System Operator spent <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 8.571 billion</span> on alternative power to replace lost output and that Electricity Distribution Lanka incurred <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 7.912 billion</span> in extra stock and maintenance costs. Penalties and performance bonds withheld totalled <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 16.989 billion</span> to offset claims.

## 6. The BOI put the Paranthan and Kankasanthurai export zones on a 2027 infrastructure timetable.

It said internal works would start in <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">January 2027</span> with land reservations at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Paranthan</span> opening to investors by end‑November 2026, alongside a proposed <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">single‑point coordination mechanism</span> and a regional manpower data centre. An investor familiarisation programme is planned to showcase sea cucumber and seaweed opportunities in the North.

## 7. Colombo Port handled 5.99 million TEUs in January–August, up 10.3% year‑on‑year on stronger transshipment.

Transshipment rose <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">10.9% to 4.83 million TEUs</span> and accounted for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">more than four‑fifths</span> of volumes, while <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">domestic boxes fell 12.5%</span> in August though were up 4.1% across eight months. Cargo handled at the four ports increased 6.5% to 90.1 million metric tonnes with ship arrivals up 5.8%.

## 8. Sri Lanka will conduct an Economic Census across 2026 and 2027.

The Department of Census and Statistics said agriculture and larger non‑agricultural establishments would be covered in 2026, with smaller <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">formal and informal</span> units surveyed in 2027 to refresh the economy’s structural map. Methodology will align with FAO’s WCA‑2020 recommendations to support <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">planning and policy</span>.

## 9. The Cabinet approved a Rs. 30,000 per hectare fertiliser subsidy for the 2026/27 Maha season.

Support is capped at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">two hectares</span> per farmer for paddy and other field crops grown on paddy lands, with a projected fiscal cost of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 16 billion</span>. The Agriculture Ministry said the programme would run on recommendations from season meetings and the Director General of Agriculture.

## 10. The Cabinet cleared 1,050 official email accounts for 350 courts under the e‑Court digitisation drive.

The Justice Ministry said the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">courts.gov.lk</span> system would include <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">voice‑to‑text</span> and video conferencing to support electronic case management and reduce delays from stenographer shortages. Hosting will use the Ministry’s platform as part of a wider transition to digital files in Magistrates’, District and High Courts.
